group_label: Group 1: Longer routes (median 12.6 km, ~7,000 weekday riders)
non_fitting_members: M12 (6.10 km, ~480 weekday riders/day) and M55 (8.16 km, ~1,210 riders/day) are shorter and carry far fewer riders than the 12.58 km / ~7,018-rider median, while M10 (8.36 km, ~1,943 riders/day) and M20 (8.30 km, ~1,813 riders/day) are mid-length routes under 2,000 riders/day; KMeans places them here because of their high weekend-to-weekday ratios (0.75–1.04) and late-night shares (11.9–15.4%).
plain_description: Longer routes (median 12.58 km, scheduled speed 10.0 km/h) averaging about 7,018 weekday riders/day (log=8.86), with the highest weekend-to-weekday ratio (0.755) and night share (13.7%), moderate peak riders per service-hour (32.45), steady weekday demand (variability=0.175), and the lowest exclusive-stop share (44.7%). Exceptions inside this group: M12 (6.10 km, ~480 riders/day), M55 (8.16 km, ~1,210 riders/day), M10 (8.36 km, ~1,943 riders/day), and M20 (8.30 km, ~1,813 riders/day) have much lower ridership and shorter lengths, but group here due to their high weekend retention (0.75–1.04) and night shares.

group_label: Group 2: Short routes with the most riders per service-hour (median 4.2 km, 66 peak riders/service-hr)
non_fitting_members: M15+ is a 13.86 km north–south Select Bus Service route (more than 3x the 4.24 km group median), yet it falls into this short-route group because its 94.2 peak riders per service-hour, ~26,160 weekday riders/day (log=10.17), low variability (0.141), and 0.583 weekend ratio match the short high-density corridors. M31 (7.09 km) and M57 (6.66 km) are also somewhat longer than the 4.24 km median.
plain_description: Short routes (median 4.24 km, scheduled speed 9.7 km/h) with the most riders per service-hour at peak (median 65.76 peak riders/service-hr, double Group 1), high weekday ridership (~6,871 riders/day, log=8.84), the lowest day-to-day demand variability (0.163), moderate weekend ratio (0.539), and 50.0% exclusive stops. Key exception: M15+ is 13.86 km long (a north–south route, not a short crosstown route), but lands here because of its 94.2 peak riders per service-hour and low variability (0.141).
